thread:
jess: quick check-in on a compact session/resume design for SDKs (py/ts/go). want to avoid huge opaque tokens but preserve safety for retries/resume. tl;dr: proposal below, please react

sam: i'm +1 on compact. main concern is cross-language ergonomics — python sync vs async vs ts streaming libs differ a lot

molly: agreed. one pattern that helped us before: a very small resume handle (<= 128 bytes) that encodes version + kind + short nonce. server keeps full state, client only passes handle

amin: question: how do we coordinate retries during resume? e.g., client crashes mid-stream and restarts with same handle — do we risk duplicate outputs?

jess: good point. two levers: idempotency keys for user requests + server-side resume idempotency window. for infer APIs we can attach an "op_id" generated by client and server dedupes within window

molly: for SDK surface: expose `session.resume(handle, opts)` and `session.create()`; avoid forcing users to mess with low-level tokens. underlying token stays opaque string but SDK validates length & shape

sam: ergonomics per-language:
- python: provide sync ``Session`` and ``AsyncSession`` wrappers that manage keepalive and refresh.
- ts: single async-first API (Promise/async iterables) since Node ecosystem prefers that.
- go: idiomatic context cancellation and a small blocking `Resume` helper

tanya: small nit: we should standardize a capability header for transports so SDK can detect server resume support and version. something like `X-Rw-Capabilities: resume=v1,streaming=1`

amin: agreed. that also helps when routing via proxies that drop weird headers — fallback path if capability absent

molly: retry/backoff interplay: if streaming connection fails, client should try resume only if server advertises `resume=v1` and the resume handle is fresh. otherwise fallback to restart with canary model or cheaper model to avoid double-charge

jess: example client pseudocode for TS to illustrate ergonomics:
```
const s = client.session.create({model: 'gpt-lite'});
for await (const chunk of s.stream()) {
  render(chunk);
}
if (s.failed && s.resumeHandle) {
  await client.session.resume(s.resumeHandle).stream();
}
```

sam: what about header limits? some infra limits header size to 8k and some to 4k. propose we cap resume handle to 1024 bytes but prefer <256 bytes. SDKs should error if handle >1024

tanya: plus we should support passing resume handle via body for very long tokens (but that's last resort). header preferred for routing performance

amin: edge case: concurrent resume attempts for same handle from different clients — need server-side lease to ensure single-writer semantics or use optimistic merge with session version in handle

molly: server lease seems simplest: resume handle includes short epoch. server atomically grants in-progress lease for N seconds, others get 409 until lease expires. SDK retries with backoff

jess: backoff sketch: jittered exponential starting at 100ms up to 10s, max attempts 6 for resume handoff. expose configurable policy on SDKs

sam: logging/observability: SDK should emit structured events: `session.create`, `session.resume.attempt`, `session.resume.success`, `session.resume.fail` with small payloads so Console can show per-token economics

molly: on pagination vs streaming: if caller needs deterministic resume semantics for discrete pages, prefer paged endpoints (cursor tokens). streaming resume is best-effort for low-latency long-running sessions

tanya: so summary decisions so far:
- compact resume handle (<256 preferred, <=1024 enforced)
- server-side full state; client only stores handle and op_id for dedupe
- capability header for transport feature negotiation
- lease-based server-side resume to avoid concurrent double-processing
- SDK ergonomics: sync/async wrappers per language; explicit session APIs
- retry/backoff policy default but configurable

sam: +1 to summary. one more: make durability explicit in SDK docs — what is guaranteed vs best-effort for streaming resume

jess: i'll draft a short follow-up RFC note with the summary and sample APIs for py/ts/go. will include migration notes for existing resume tokens. anyone want to take co-author?

molly: i'll co-author and add test harness ideas (chaos tests for mid-stream crash + resume)

deploy-bot: auto-deploy scheduled: rfc-drafts/compact-session-resume.md -> staging at 2026-04-01T09:00Z :rocket:

jess: thanks all. feel free to drop design comments inline on the draft when I post it later today :thumbsup:
